newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM says hostage talks may begin next week.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM says hostage talks may begin next week.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Friday that the Peruvian government and Marxist rebels could begin preliminary talks next week to end the hostage crisis in Lima.
"I have a feeling that (preliminary talks) may get going next week," Hashimoto told ruling party leaders.
Peru's President Alberto Fujimori promised Hashimoto last weekend that he would resume direct talks with Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's home.
But he has insisted he would not give in to the rebels' demand that some 400 jailed comrades be freed.
Mediators held a meeting on Thursday with Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, leader of the Marxist rebels, to try to persuade him to resume talks to end the 51-day siege.

"I hope that with the participation of everyone we will find that light of a peaceful solution," Roman Catholic Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani told reporters outside the residence, where he spent 2-1/2 hours along with Red Cross representative Michel Minnig and Canadian Ambassador Anthony Vincent.

They are part of a four-member panel of "guarantors" for eventual talks between Cerpa and chief government negotiator Domingo Palermo, who have not held face-to-face talks since December 28. The fourth, Japanese representative Terusuke Tarada, was not present on Thursday.
Cipriani said the hostages, held by about 15 armed Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas since December 17, were holding up well.

The MRTA has released most of the nearly 500 VIP captives it seized when it stormed a garden party at the residence seven weeks ago. But it has held on to its most valuable hostages, including two government ministers.
